correctness.rationale: Strict convexity and entropy derivative at zero prove existence and interior uniqueness. KKT yields exactly F(t)=b+lambda*t with F decreasing. Uniform t=O(log 1/lambda), t->infinity, and minimal-weight exponential asymptotics rigorously imply both data/regularization regimes. At b=0 Lambert W monotonicity gives an explicit relative remainder O(exp(-delta*W(B/lambda))) and exact equality when all coefficients agree. Shape and non-Lipschitz conclusions follow. CHECK.py tests 39 systems with KKT residuals <1e-70; finite checks are not used as proof.

value.rationale: Joint small-data/small-regularization sensitivity in positive inverse reconstruction is materially different from fixed-signal or fixed-mass convergence. The scale lambda log(1/lambda) separates two different leading constants, and distinct forward weights create a full noninteger power hierarchy despite positive priors. This pinpoints continuation/underflow regimes and the loss of endpoint Lipschitz stability in a canonical one-measurement model, rather than merely calculating a generic scalar entropy minimizer.
